Koah Sharpe had been missing since Monday when he was taken by his father, Michael Comer, 25, according to the Lexington County Sheriff's Department. Comer was arrested on a burglary charge on Monday evening but his son was not with him. Sharpe was found on Tuesday "buried alive" and "clinging to life" not far from his father's house, Lexington County Sheriff Jay Koon said at a news conference. It is thought he had been there for 24 hours.

stories.summary: LIV Golf filed a Chapter 11 bankruptcy plan with a New Jersey court Tuesday, along with a proposed schedule for a final hearing on its disclosure statement on Jan. 7 that would begin liquidation. LIV Golf filed for bankruptcy on Sept. 8 after the Public Investment Fund of Saudi Arabia, which had bankrolled the breakaway league from the start, said a change in strategy meant it would no longer pay for LIV after the 2026 season. The bankruptcy plan is for an orderly wind down of LIV. The restructuring agreement with BC Partners Credit, which had pledged $300 million, failed to garner enough support for a LIV 2.0 version that would have kept the league going in 2027.

Leonardo Bertulazzi used a harness to abseil down from a fifth-floor balcony in the capital, Buenos Aires. Shaheen played for head coach Rocky Bourquin. His dad, Joe, played for Tim Miller, a program icon who spent 25 years as the Wildcats' skipper. Mike Shaheen suffered a serious injury in an outfield collision in his senior year of 2003 but came back to play for a South team that fell in the tournament to eventual state runner-up Central Catholic.

stories.title: When rain finally does come to drylands, only some microbes in the soil 'awaken'
stories.summary: In arid regions, the microbes that power threatened dryland soil ecosystems called biological soil crusts stay dormant over long periods, only "awakening" when they sense moisture from infrequent rainfall. Now, a team led by researchers at Penn State—driven by projections that those biocrusts will decline by as much as 40% in the next 45 years—found that when a dryland soil does get wet, most of the microbes in the biocrust stay inactive. It's a discovery that will inform ongoing efforts to conserve and restore biocrusts, according to the researchers.
